Send the order to the exchange with the order ID.

If sending to the exchange fails, move the order to a dead letter.
Idempotency check: if the cancellation is already processed, do nothing and proceed.
Send the cancellation of the order to the exchange.
Two instances must never submit the same order twice to the exchange API. orderId is the
idempotency key, and the service performs an idempotency check before calling the
exchange: an atomic write with a strict guard condition.
0 rows → already claimed or processed elsewhere → skip, commit the offset.
1 row → this consumer owns the order and calls the exchange.
Same pattern for cancel: pending_cancel → cancelling.
Why it works: the row-level lock makes check + write atomic, so two consumers cannot
Also: the exchange call carries the order ID as the client / idempotency key, so even a
duplicate call is ignored by the exchange.
Query the exchange with the idempotency key.
Order found: the request reached the exchange, but the dispatch service failed to
update the DB. Fill in the current status (submitted, filled or partially_filled) and
the externalOrderId; update the metadata store if necessary.
Order not found: update the DB with status "failed".
Query the exchange with the idempotency key.
Cancelled at the exchange: update the local DB to cancelled.
Still active: ensure the cancellation and set the status to cancelled.
Filled before the cancellation was processed: update the DB to filled or
User can see live prices of stocks.
User can manage orders of stocks.
High availability for price updates with eventual consistency.
(The user should always be able to see stock prices and movements, but it is okay for
prices to be stale for some seconds.)
(It is okay for the user not to be able to place an order for some time, but an order
must never be in an inconsistent state.)
Low latency for reflecting stock prices (under 200 ms) and for placing orders.
Scalability: 10 million daily active users, 5 trades per user per day, 1000s
Read-heavy system: stock price updates >> trade orders.
Minimize active connections to the external exchange API.
(Calls to the external exchange API are expensive.)
